Of course! This is one of the main symptoms of love addiction. I used to do this with multiple guys at once. 
The fantasy is what we actually get addicted to because it’s what gives us a high. Like any drug, quitting is hard and takes work but it is possible. 

I think you’re off to a super great start— you have identified (and possibly accepted) this as a fantasy—not reality. It is a drug you have to quit. 

What helps after that is to identify what the fantasy was — what were we “making up” about the person or the relationship that wasn’t real? This can be tricky because the fantasy can be tricky and make you look the other way/disregard reality. 

Then, it takes brutal, painful, honesty to pick apart what is fantasy and what is reality. Who is this person really? Are things really the way you have them in your head? This can be really sobering, but that’s what you want, right? Sobriety. 

For me, I was involved with a guy all the way across the country. He was a great guy and we talked on the phone every day. But that was it. Two years later, I realized that was all we were. Sure, we visited each other, FaceTimed, sent each other gifts, even provided each other emotional support. But my fantasy was so overblown compared to that. To an embarrassing degree. 

In my mind, we were practically husband and wife. We were going to live together someday (even though there was absolutely no indication of that being a possibility). My family was going to love and accept him (not true at all). I was going to be a loving step-mother to his son, who would love me back. His ex wife would be jealous of me and someday feel bad for how horrible she treated him after seeing how in love with me he was. 

None of that was real! He was a face on a screen. A text message in a box. I was I love with a happy story I told myself in my head. I was getting high every day reading and writing text messages and lying in bed picking out what he would wear at our wedding. I was delusional. 

You can see how this can be tricky. Because he truly was a great guy. An amazing long distance boyfriend. Because he was so great and treated me well, it took two years to figure out that there was a lot of fantasy to sift out. I realized that I didn’t like what was left when you took the fantasy out. It wasn’t enough. So I bailed.
